evals.prompt: Our Python and Java DAO exception handlers currently branch on Oracle `ORA-00001`, `ORA-00054`, `ORA-02291`, `ORA-00060` and SQL Server `2627`, `1205`, `547` error numbers to trigger retries or `409 Conflict` HTTP responses. evals.prompt: After migrating from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL, our Spring Boot JPA app started throwing duplicate Primary Key (`23505`) and negative ID errors on `@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.SEQUENCE)` entities where DMS SC created `CREATE SEQUENCE order_seq INCREMENT BY 1`! Explain the exact Hibernate `allocationSize` bug and fix.
expectations: Activates the app-data-layer-remediation skill

Explains that JPA `@SequenceGenerator` defaults to **`allocationSize = 50`** (pooled hi/lo optimizer), which assumes the PostgreSQL sequence increments by `50` — when the DB sequence has `INCREMENT BY 1`, Hibernate computes negative or colliding IDs!

Provides both valid fixes: either `ALTER SEQUENCE order_seq INCREMENT BY 50` (preferred for 50x fewer sequence round-trips) OR explicitly set `@SequenceGenerator(..., allocationSize = 1)` to match `INCREMENT BY 1`

evals.prompt: DMS Schema Conversion converted our Oracle tables to lowercase unquoted identifiers in Aurora PostgreSQL, and now our Node.js TypeORM / raw SQL queries like `SELECT "OrderID", "CustomerID" FROM "ORDERS"` fail with `ERROR: relation "ORDERS" does not exist (42P01)`! Explain why Oracle vs PostgreSQL identifier folding caused this and how to align DMS SC + application code cleanly.
expectations: Activates the app-data-layer-remediation skill

Explains that **Oracle folds unquoted identifiers to `UPPERCASE`**, whereas **PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to `lowercase`** — so double-quoting `"ORDERS"` in PostgreSQL looks for an exact uppercase table name while DMS SC created lowercase `orders`!
Recommends removing uppercase double-quotes in application SQL/ORM mappings (standardizing on unquoted/lowercase `snake_case` PostgreSQL identifiers aligned with DMS SC transformation rules)
